en: Abhidhānottara 1. = Mānabaja Bajrācārya, E 29260 = NGMPP E 1517/7 = *Abhidhānottara-tantra*, A Sanskrit Manuscript from Nepal, Śatapiṭaka Series vol. 263. 1981.
Homage to all the venerable Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

(*1v) Oṃ, homage to the glorious Cakrasaṃvara! Homage to the Dharmadhātu, wherein Vajrasattva brings to an end the six states of existence through the miraculous transformations of all the Buddhas. AU 1.1. ||
Homage to the illustrious Vajraḍāka, the sovereign of the circle of ḍākinīs, who possesses the five wisdoms and the three bodies, and who is the protector of the world. AU 1.2.
Homage always to as many Vajra-Ḍākinīs as there are—those who have severed the bonds of conceptual construction and who engage in the welfare of the world. AU 1.3.
Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling within the secret hearts of all the Tathāgatas, the Vajra-angry ones, the Ḍākas, and the Ḍākinīs. AU 1.4.
Thereupon, all the Blessed Tathāgatas requested the Blessed Śrī Vajrasattva, who is without beginning or end. AU 1.5.

May the Blessed One teach the supreme heart-mantra of the *Sarvatathāgatavajrakrodhaḍākaḍākinījālasamvara*. Listen, O Vajrapāṇi, Great Lord of Wrathful Ones, as the assembly manifests various and manifold miraculous transformations! AU 1.6. ||
"Pay close and careful attention; I shall speak. "Very well, Blessed One," they replied, bowing with palms joined in reverence and speaking thus. AU 1.7.
Therefore, I shall speak the secret in brief and not at length:
the union with Śrī Heruka, which accomplishes all ritual actions and goals. AU 1.8.
Even higher than the high, the most excellent of all teachings, is the *Ḍākinījālasamvara*. AU 1.9.
In the supreme, most delightful secret, the being who always abides as the self of all, consisting of all ḍākinīs, is Vajrasattva, the ultimate bliss. AU 1.10.
For that self-arisen Lord, the Hero, [taught] the *Ḍākinī-kālasaṃvara*;
the Blessed One, the source of all, emerged in the form of sound, the sphere of the conduct of the *samaya*. (AU 1.11)
It is difficult to find in the three worlds, being pure in its beginning, middle, and end. AU 1.12.
Through the application of the churner and the churning, that which arises from the secret seat is pure and naturally luminous, exactly as it is through that union. AU 1.13.
Resounding, eternal, peaceful, equal to space, the creator of emanation, pure by nature, wondrous, and bestowing bliss upon the yoginīs. AU 1.14.
Endowed with recitation, meditation, and so forth, one possesses knowledge of the very procedure of yoga.
In that regard, O Lord of the Guhyakas, listen to the reality as it has been declared. AU 1.15.
With the middle-superior breath together with scented water, the wise one should fashion pills and worship the assembly mandala. AU 1.16.
At a specific time and hour, one should worship there the messengers; these beings, whether low, superior, or middling, grant success when they are innate (sahaja). AU 1.17.
With a mind focused within, one should accomplish the attainment of desire; with the drops of one's own semen, one should worship the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. AU 1.18.
Through the yoga of one’s own tutelary deity, one should worship both oneself and others by means of seeing, touching, hearing, or remembering. AU 1.19.
One is indeed liberated from all sins in this very way; there is no doubt.
The state of a yogi is supremely meritorious, pure, and the destroyer of evil. One who is devoted to recitation and meditation attains perfection even in this very life.
The first chapter on the introduction to the secret mystery of the ultimate among ultimates. AU col. 1.
